AUTOMATED RECONCILIATION

Ledger ↔ Bank Reconciliation Engine

Reconciles a merchant's internal ledger against the bank settlement statement. Deterministic rules resolve the large majority of transactions; a language model is reserved for the small number of cases that require genuine judgment.

Engineering validation

Three issues identified and corrected during development, each verified against the labeled ground-truth dataset rather than assumed fixed.

Matching complexity at scale
The original matching logic compared every record against every other record — adequate at small volume, but degrading sharply past a few thousand transactions. Replaced with indexed lookups keyed on each pass's match fields.
2,616 records/sec
252,000+ /sec
Duplicate detection was not genuine
The classification model appeared to detect duplicate bookings, but was in fact keying off a synthetic identifier left in the test-data generator rather than real transaction signal. Replaced with a deterministic structural check.
looked accurate
100% verified
Fee-tolerance band miscalibrated
The fee-matching tolerance was wide enough to also accept genuine payment discrepancies as clean fee deductions. Tightened to match the actual observed fee distribution.
91% wrongly accepted
11% (known, explained)
A note on the match-rate figure
An earlier iteration reported an 87% match rate. That figure included transactions later identified as false matches under an overly permissive fee-tolerance rule. The corrected rate — 80% — is verified against a labeled ground-truth dataset. A lower, verified figure is worth more than a higher, unverified one.
